title: Reverse Linked List
statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.

mistakes.hint1: Are you losing the rest of the list when you change a pointer?
mistakes.hint2: When you do `curr->next = prev`, you detach `curr` from the remaining nodes.
mistakes.hint3: You need to store the next node before you overwrite `curr->next`.
mistakes.hint4: Use a temporary pointer: `ListNode* nextTemp = curr->next;` before reversing.

mistakes.hint1: What did you initialize your `prev` pointer to?
mistakes.hint2: If you initialized it to a new node or `head`, it will create a cycle or extra node.
mistakes.hint3: The new tail of the reversed list needs to point to NULL.

mistakes.hint1: Which pointer are you returning at the end of the function?
mistakes.hint2: If you return `head` or `curr`, they might be pointing to NULL or the old start.
mistakes.hint3: You want to return the new head of the reversed list.
mistakes.hint4: Return the `prev` pointer, as it holds the last processed node.

mistakes.hint1: Check the direction you are pointing the arrows.
mistakes.hint2: You want `curr->next` to point backwards to `prev`.

mistakes.hint1: What happens if the list is completely empty (head is NULL)?
mistakes.hint2: What if there is only 1 node in the list?
mistakes.hint3: Does your code throw a Segmentation Fault?
mistakes.hint4: Add `if (!head || !head->next) return head;` at the very beginning.

mistakes.hint3: If you didn't save the next node, you might be looping back on yourself.
mistakes.hint4: Ensure you do `curr = nextTemp;` at the end of every iteration.

mistakes.hint1: Are you moving your pointers in the right order?
mistakes.hint2: If you move `curr` before reversing the link, you break the chain.
mistakes.hint3: The order of operations is crucial here.
mistakes.hint4: Order: 1. save next, 2. reverse link, 3. update prev, 4. advance curr.
